title: Certified rational Jacobian torsion
objective: Implement certified rational torsion upper/lower/exact records for genus-2/3 hyperelliptic Jacobians using good-prime reduction and verified supplied Mumford divisors

oracles: SageMath and direct finite-field reduction fixtures
certificate replay and exact Jacobian arithmetic

handoff.summary: Added an ordinary strict-Python certified rational-torsion engine for odd-degree genus-2/3 Jacobians over QQ. It computes residue-characteristic-correct good-reduction upper bounds with fully replayed algorithm/search/skipped-prime certificates and progressive histories, exact branch-factor rational 2-torsion with generators, canonical QQ Mumford serialization, and exact supplied-divisor order proofs. Supplied input sequences are retained and deterministically replayed into the returned invariant-factor basis; reduction witnesses distinguish nonintegral representatives from unsupported operations and check divisibility by #J(F_p) plus the p-primary specialization kernel. The full group is claimed only when lower equals upper. Focused tests include PARI-pinned local polynomials, an explicit rational order-3 divisor with dependent/duplicate supplied inputs, primary-bound properties, and certificate tampering.
risks: No bounded search for previously unknown odd torsion is included; callers must supply odd-torsion divisors.
Automatic local-factor verification uses the available auto backend, with exhaustive dynamic fallback; very large explicit verification primes can therefore be expensive without a native backend.

Broad native/platform validation is intentionally deferred to the integration lane per coordinator direction; the source has no native-only dependency and direct Pyright plus focused dynamic tests pass.
next_steps: Integration lane should add public HyperellipticJacobian torsion_bound/torsion_subgroup methods and strict-module registry entries.
Integration lane should consume exact/lower/upper status in BSD arithmetic without treating a bounded result as an exact torsion order.
Run centralized Linux, WebAssembly, Windows, and macOS validation after the shared public wiring lands.
